s1.syndrome_frame: Gradual onset of a painless, firm, and nonpulsatile mass in the thigh, fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin, with no signs of inflammation or neurovascular impairment
salient_findings: Painless swelling in the left medial thigh
Firm, nonpulsatile mass fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin
Well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass on CT scan with internal septations and density similar to subcutaneous fat
key_facts: Swelling in the left medial thigh
Mass enlarged gradually over six months
No history of trauma or infection
Firm, nonpulsatile mass measuring approximately 10 cm
No signs of inflammation, neurovascular impairment, or inguinal lymphadenopathy
CT scan showed a well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass in the left anteromedial compartment of the proximal thigh
MRI confirmed a fatty-appearing, well-circumscribed mass with internal septations and no encasement of neurovascular structures

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Fatty-appearing mass with internal septations on MRI, consistent with lipoma characteristics

shortlist.label: Liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely due to the well-circumscribed nature, liposarcoma remains a consideration given the large size of the mass

shortlist.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of a firm, nonpulsatile mass with internal septations could be consistent with fibrolipomatous hamartoma

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: The description of the mass as firm and nonpulsatile with a fatty appearance on MRI could suggest pleomorphic lipoma

shortlist.label: Atypical lipomatous tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Given the large size and gradual growth of the mass, atypical lipomatous tumor is a plausible, though less common, consideration

raw.rationale: The presence of a firm, nonpulsatile mass with internal septations and a density similar to subcutaneous fat, as shown on CT and MRI scans, is consistent with fibrolipomatous hamartoma, a benign tumor composed of mature fat and fibrous tissue.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: While lipoma is a fatty tumor, the presence of internal septations and the specific location and characteristics of the mass are more suggestive of fibrolipomatous hamartoma.

rejected.label: Liposarcoma
rejected.why: Liposarcoma is a malignant tumor that would likely show more aggressive features, such as invasion of surrounding tissues or lymphadenopathy, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Pleomorphic lipoma
rejected.why: Pleomorphic lipoma is a rare, benign tumor that typically occurs in the subcutaneous tissue of the neck or shoulder region, which does not match the location of the mass in this case.

rejected.label: Atypical lipomatous tumor
rejected.why: Atypical lipomatous tumor is a malignant tumor that would likely show more aggressive features, such as invasion of surrounding tissues or lymphadenopathy, which are not present in this case.
